label: Ticket Inbox
description: The continuous stream of inbound support tickets across channels - email, web form, chat - arriving with no fixed shape. The raw input the whole triage workflow starts from.

lesson.intent: Inspect where tickets arrive, in what channels and shape, and tag the fields triage depends on in one raw ticket.

labVersion: Inspected by you in the Ticket Inbox task; the tickets are local fixtures shared with the Ticket Record task.
accessNeeded: Read access to the support channels
soloRebuildPath: Start with a folder of local ticket fixtures
Tag the fields triage needs: who, what, when, channel
Later ingest from the helpdesk API
governanceNote: Tickets arrive from many channels with no schedule; the intake queue is the single place triage reads, so nothing is worked from a personal inbox.
auditNote: Inspection by tagging (tagSource): the learner tags the ticket's spans that become the record's fields, the where-the-structure-comes-from moment.

label: Ticket Record
description: A trusted structured record extracted from one customer ticket: id, reporter, channel, product area, and the reported symptom. The record every triage step reads instead of the raw prose.

lesson.intent: Extract the fields triage acts on from a customer ticket's prose into a validated ticket record.

labVersion: Built by you in the Ticket Record task from a ticket fixture in the inbox.
accessNeeded: Write access to the ticket system
soloRebuildPath: Hand-key the fields from one ticket into JSON
Add extraction from known form fields
Later wire NLP extraction with human review
governanceNote: The extracted record is what triage trusts instead of the customer's prose; its field definitions must be owned and stable.
auditNote: Build lesson; classification, priority, and routing all read this record rather than the raw ticket.

label: Intent Taxonomy
description: The governed category tree tickets are classified against: billing, bug, how-to, outage, and their sub-categories. The single source for what a ticket can be, owned by Support Ops.

lesson.intent: Read the intent taxonomy as governed reference data: the category tree, who may change it, and why classification must map to it, not to free text.

labVersion: Provided as a local taxonomy fixture the classification task maps against.
soloRebuildPath: Start with a local category tree
Record who owns each category and its definition
Later integrate with the helpdesk taxonomy
governanceNote: The Support Ops Analyst owns the taxonomy; classification maps to its categories, never to invented free-text labels, so reporting and routing stay consistent.
auditNote: Governance lesson; the temporal loop (triage-archive -> intent-taxonomy) tunes this taxonomy from real misroutes.

label: Classification
description: Assigning each ticket a category from the governed taxonomy by interpreting the customer's words. The human-text-to-structured-signal step, done at volume.

lesson.intent: Interpret a ticket's prose and assign the correct taxonomy category, distinguishing the reported symptom from the customer's guessed cause.

labVersion: Assigned by you in the Classification task against the ticket record and taxonomy fixtures.
accessNeeded: A place to record the category
soloRebuildPath: Read the ticket and pick the taxonomy category
Separate the symptom from the customer's guess
Later add an ML classifier with human review
governanceNote: Classify the symptom the customer reports, not the cause they guess; a wrong category at volume is the root of most misroutes.
auditNote: Interpretation lesson (choiceCheck); the category the customer names is often a distractor for the real one.

label: Priority Matrix
description: The governed 4x4 grid that maps impact (how many, how badly) against urgency (how fast) to a priority P1-P4. The owned config that makes priority a rule, not a mood.

lesson.intent: Read the priority matrix as owned, versioned config: impact by urgency yields a priority, so an angry customer with low impact is not automatically a P1.

labVersion: Provided as a local priority-matrix fixture the priority task applies.
accessNeeded: Support Ops Analyst approval for changes
soloRebuildPath: Start with a 4x4 impact-by-urgency grid
Version it and record who approved each change
Later integrate with the helpdesk priority config
governanceNote: Priority is matrix-derived and auditable; a looser matrix moves tickets faster but floods the P1 queue - the trade-off is a governed decision.
auditNote: Governance lesson; the hard tier deepens this into designing the matrix from incident history.

label: Priority Assignment
description: Applying the matrix to a ticket's impact and urgency to derive its priority, including the boundary cases where an emotional ticket scores lower than it feels.

lesson.intent: Read a ticket's impact and urgency and apply the matrix to derive its priority, defending the P1 boundary against pressure.

labVersion: Run by you in the Priority Assignment task using the classification and priority-matrix fixtures.
accessNeeded: A place to record the priority
soloRebuildPath: Read impact and urgency from the ticket
Look up the priority in the matrix
Later wire the priority automation
governanceNote: A P1 comes from the matrix, not the customer's tone; recording impact and urgency separately keeps the derivation auditable.
auditNote: Transformation; the medium tier scores a P1-looking ticket as P3 to teach the boundary.

label: Routing Table
description: The governed mapping from category and priority to a destination queue. The owned config that turns a classified, prioritized ticket into a routing decision.

lesson.intent: Read the routing table as owned config: category plus priority maps to exactly one queue, so routing is a lookup, not a judgement call.

labVersion: Provided as a local routing-table fixture the route decision applies.
soloRebuildPath: Start with a category+priority -> queue table
Keep queue names to the governed list
Later integrate with the helpdesk routing engine
governanceNote: The Queue Lead owns the routing table; queue names come only from it, so a ticket is never routed to a queue that does not exist.
auditNote: Governance lesson; the hard tier adds load-shedding rules when a queue is over SLA.

label: Route Decision
description: The fork: a P1 or safety-flagged ticket escalates to Tier-2/Duty; everything else routes to its standard queue by the routing table. The single decision node of the map.

lesson.intent: Encode the routing rule: escalate P1 or safety-flagged tickets; route the rest to their table queue by category and priority.

labVersion: Encoded by you in the Route Decision task from the classification, priority, and routing table.
soloRebuildPath: Escalate when priority is P1 or a safety flag is set
Otherwise look up the queue in the routing table
Later wire it into the workflow engine
governanceNote: The rule must be explicit and logged; a P1 escalates even if its queue is busy, and a non-P1 never jumps the escalation path.
auditNote: The single decision node (the fork). Hard tier is the solo-rebuild capstone (artifactImport).

label: Escalation Handoff
description: The P1 path: page Tier-2 or the Duty Manager, capture the acknowledgement, and log who owns the outage. A high-priority handoff that must not be silent.

lesson.intent: Work a P1 escalation: page the right owner, capture their acknowledgement, and log the handoff so an outage is never sitting unowned.

labVersion: Worked by you in the Escalation Handoff task; the P1 rides from the route-decision result.
accessNeeded: A place to log the acknowledgement
soloRebuildPath: Page the Tier-2 Engineer or Duty Manager
Capture who acknowledged and when
Later wire the on-call paging tool
governanceNote: Every P1 escalation captures who acknowledged it; a paged alert with no acknowledgement is an outage nobody owns.
auditNote: Handoff (handoffForm) with captured acknowledgement; the P1 branch of the fork.

label: Queue Assignment
description: The standard path: assign the ticket to its routing-table queue and log the assignment. Even the quiet path records where a ticket went and who owns it.

lesson.intent: Assign a standard ticket to its queue and record the assignment, so the routine path is as traceable as the escalation path.

labVersion: Recorded by you in the Queue Assignment task from a standard-routed ticket.
soloRebuildPath: Assign the ticket to its table queue
Log the queue and the assignment time
Later wire skills-based assignment
governanceNote: Standard does not mean unlogged; the routine lane must be as auditable as escalation (echoes Meridian's routine path).
auditNote: Handoff (handoffForm); deliberately mirrors the module pattern that the quiet path still produces a record.

label: SLA Tracker
description: Timers per queue and priority: how long a ticket has until its SLA breach, and a flag when it has. The signal the digest reports and load-shedding acts on.

lesson.intent: Apply per-priority SLA targets to each ticket and flag whether it is within SLA or breached.

labVersion: Run by you in the SLA Tracker task against the routed tickets and the SLA targets.
accessNeeded: A place to record breach flags
soloRebuildPath: Compute elapsed time against the SLA target
Flag within-SLA or breached per ticket
Later wire the SLA timer service
governanceNote: SLA targets are per priority (a P1 clock is minutes, a P4 is days); a breach flag with no target behind it is meaningless.
auditNote: Transformation via jsonDeltas rows (ticketId/withinSla/breachFlag); breaches feed the digest.

label: Resolution Record
description: The outcome captured when a ticket is resolved: the fix, and the category it turned out to be when actually worked. The record misroute detection compares against.

lesson.intent: Capture a ticket's resolution: the fix applied and the category-as-worked, which may differ from the category it was assigned.

labVersion: Built by you in the Resolution Record task from a worked ticket.
accessNeeded: The taxonomy for the worked category
soloRebuildPath: Record the fix and the category it was actually
Keep the same taxonomy for the worked category
Later capture it at ticket close automatically
governanceNote: The category-as-worked is the ground truth; capturing it honestly - even when it differs from the assignment - is what makes misroute detection possible.
auditNote: Build lesson; feeds the misroute check that compares worked vs assigned category.

label: Misroute Check
description: Comparing the category a ticket was assigned to the category it was actually worked as. A mismatch is a misroute - the signal that tunes the taxonomy.

lesson.intent: Compare the assigned category to the worked category and flag a misroute when they differ.

labVersion: Run by you in the Misroute Check task from the classification and resolution records.
accessNeeded: A place to record the misroute flag
soloRebuildPath: Compare assigned and worked categories
Flag a misroute when they differ
Later feed misroutes to taxonomy review
governanceNote: A misroute is not blame - it is data; a category that is repeatedly misrouted is a taxonomy problem, not an agent problem.
auditNote: Transformation; misroutes feed both the digest and, via the archive, the taxonomy-feedback loop.

label: Queue Digest
description: The 5:00 PM queue-health digest: volumes, misroutes, SLA breaches, and taxonomy drift, assembled from the day's triage records. The module's deliverable.

lesson.intent: Assemble the queue-health digest from the day's records: volume, misroutes, and SLA breaches, by lookup from stored artifacts.

labVersion: Assembled by you in the Queue Digest task from the SLA tracker and misroute check.
accessNeeded: A delivery channel for the digest
soloRebuildPath: Total the volumes, misroutes, and breaches
Assemble them into the digest document
Later generate and send it on a schedule
governanceNote: The digest is only trustworthy if every number traces to a triage record; a hand-tuned figure is a report nobody can audit.
auditNote: The assembly node and the module deliverable (queue-digest.md); templateSlots renders it from canon values.

label: Triage Archive
description: The retained record of the day's triage: records, digest, and misroutes. It preserves the day for audit and feeds the taxonomy tuning that keeps classification honest.

lesson.intent: Archive the day's triage for retention and export the misroutes that tomorrow's taxonomy review reads.

labVersion: Archived by you in the Triage Archive task from the completed digest.
soloRebuildPath: Write the day's triage to a dated archive
Export misroutes to the taxonomy review
Later integrate with the analytics warehouse
governanceNote: Retention length is a compliance decision; the archive is also the loop input, so the taxonomy improves from real misroutes.
auditNote: The archive origin of the temporal loop (triage-archive -> intent-taxonomy), refined by taxonomy-feedback.

label: Taxonomy Feedback
description: What the misroutes teach the taxonomy: a category that keeps getting reworked needs splitting, renaming, or a clearer definition. The proposal that closes the triage loop.

lesson.intent: Turn the archived misroutes into a taxonomy change proposal: identify the category that fails and propose the fix, routed to the owner.

labVersion: Run by you in the Taxonomy Feedback task from the triage archive fixture.
soloRebuildPath: Find the category with repeated misroutes
Propose a split, rename, or clearer definition
Later feed reclassification trends automatically
governanceNote: Taxonomy changes still go through Support Ops governance; feedback proposes, it does not silently rewrite the category tree.
auditNote: Closes the temporal loop into intent-taxonomy; classification systems are maintained, not installed.
